request_path.label: Cloudflare sits between a visitor and a website
request_path.description: A visitor sends a request to Cloudflare. Within the simplified request path, the web application firewall inspects it before permitted work continues toward the website's origin server. This diagram omits caching and other services. It does not say every request reaches an origin.
request_path.caption: Conceptual request path. A shared processing step can affect many unrelated websites.
request_path.source:
@startuml
layout vertical
component Visitor
component Cloudflare
component WAF
component Origin
Visitor --> Cloudflare : request
Cloudflare --> WAF : inspect
WAF --> Origin : continue
@enduml

observations.label: Symptoms and observations localize the investigation
observations.description: Requests reach Cloudflare's request workers. Observations identify exhausted serving CPU and activity in the web application firewall. Front-line servers return 502 errors to visitors. This is a synthesis of observations, not an instrument trace or a complete server topology.
observations.caption: By 14:00 UTC, CPU observations, traces, and logs implicated the WAF. A component location is still short of a full diagnosis.
observations.source:
@startuml
layout vertical
component Requests
component RequestWorkers
component WAF
component FrontLine
component Visitors
Requests --> RequestWorkers : work arrives
RequestWorkers --> WAF : activity implicated
note right of RequestWorkers : Serving CPU exhausted
FrontLine --> Visitors : 502 errors
@enduml

rollout.label: A rule change reaches request processing worldwide
rollout.description: An approved rule passes build and functional tests, then Quicksilver distributes it to the WAF across the network. Incoming requests independently reach the WAF for evaluation. Simulate mode changes the action taken on a match, but whether evaluating this rule is expensive remains the question.
rollout.caption: Configuration distribution and request processing are different paths. A rule update can change computation without a server-binary release.
rollout.source:
@startuml
layout vertical
component ApprovedRule
component FunctionalTests
component Quicksilver
component WAF
component Requests
ApprovedRule --> FunctionalTests : build and test
FunctionalTests --> Quicksilver : publish rule
Quicksilver --> WAF : global configuration
Requests --> WAF : evaluate rule
@enduml

blocked_progress.label: Evaluation can consume resources before any blocking decision
blocked_progress.description: A request worker invokes WAF inspection, which calls the pattern matcher. Matching consumes excessive CPU and the worker does not make useful request progress in this simplified sequence. The front line returns 502 to the visitor. No deliberate WAF block decision is shown, and the sequence does not claim a recovered per-request timeout trace.
blocked_progress.caption: Causal reconstruction of the resource dependency. Simulating a rule's action still requires computing its match.
blocked_progress.source:
@startuml
actor visitor: Visitor
participant front: Front line
participant worker: Request worker
participant waf: WAF
participant matcher: Matcher
visitor -> front: request page
front -> worker: handle request
worker -> waf: inspect
waf -> matcher: evaluate pattern
matcher -> matcher: excessive matching work
note over worker: Useful progress impaired
front --> visitor: 502 error
@enduml

recovery.label: Availability returns before WAF protection is restored
recovery.description: The service moves from unavailable to traffic recovered after global WAF termination. At the traffic-recovered state the WAF remains disabled; an outgoing transition toward WAF restoration still requires evidence. These states summarize the service response, not Cloudflare's software state machine.
recovery.caption: 14:07 UTC: global WAF termination. By 14:09: traffic and CPU recovered. Restoring the security function is a separate obligation.
recovery.source:
@startuml
state Unavailable
state TrafficRecovered
state WAFRestored
Unavailable --> TrafficRecovered : terminate WAF
TrafficRecovered --> WAFRestored : evidence still required
note right of TrafficRecovered : WAF remains disabled
@enduml

causal_test.label: A controlled comparison tests the candidate rule
causal_test.description: An investigator evaluates the WAF without the candidate rule, with the candidate rule, and after removing it again, comparing outcomes under controlled conditions. Outcomes are deliberately not supplied here. The diagram represents a proposed experiment; it is not a transcript of historical commands.
causal_test.caption: Keep input and environment comparable while varying the candidate cause. Confine any risky replay to an isolated setting.
causal_test.source:
@startuml
actor investigator: Investigator
participant setup: Isolated setup
participant observer: Measurements
investigator -> setup: candidate absent
setup -> observer: record outcome
investigator -> setup: candidate present
setup -> observer: record outcome
investigator -> setup: candidate removed again
setup -> observer: record outcome
@enduml

outcomes.label: Matching answers and resource outcomes are different
outcomes.description: In a proposed bounded experiment, evaluating a pattern can find a match, exhaust all candidates and report no match, or require another check after using the allowed budget. Only the first two are matching answers. The bounded experiment stops before performing a disallowed check. Budget exceeded is a resource outcome, not a negative matching answer.
outcomes.caption: Teaching test contract. The budget and these states are not recovered production safeguards.
outcomes.source:
@startuml
state Evaluating
state Match
state NoMatch
state BudgetExceeded
[*] --> Evaluating
Evaluating --> Match : pattern found
Evaluating --> NoMatch : candidates exhausted
Evaluating --> BudgetExceeded : another check needed beyond budget
@enduml

repeated_candidates.label: Different allocations can retry the same missing character
repeated_candidates.description: The teaching matcher starts at the beginning of xxx. A first skip and a second skip can each consume any number of characters. With skip lengths three and zero, it tests for equals at the end and fails. With lengths two and one it tests the same end again and fails. With lengths two and zero it tests before the last x and fails. More allocations remain. These are three illustrative attempts, not the full production regex.
repeated_candidates.caption: Teaching trace: two overlapping skips followed by a required equals sign. The input xxx contains no equals sign.
repeated_candidates.source:
@startuml
participant choices: Skip lengths
participant check: Equals check
participant input: Input xxx
choices -> check: first 3, second 0
check -> input: test at end
input --> check: missing equals
choices -> check: first 2, second 1
check -> input: test at same end
input --> check: missing equals
choices -> check: first 2, second 0
check -> input: test before last x
input --> check: missing equals
note over choices: More allocations remain
@enduml

allocation_tree.label: Ten allocations for only three characters
allocation_tree.description: For a three-character input and a fixed starting position, first-skip length three leaves one possible second-skip length, length two leaves two, length one leaves three, and length zero leaves four. These branches total ten checks for the required equals sign. Every check fails on xxx. Counts are for this explicit teaching model, not PCRE instructions.
allocation_tree.caption: The search repeats work because several allocations reach the same input position. The branch counts are 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.
allocation_tree.source:
@startuml
participant first: First skip
participant second: Second skip
first -> second: length 3 leaves 0 characters
second --> first: 1 possible length
first -> second: length 2 leaves 1 character
second --> first: 2 possible lengths
first -> second: length 1 leaves 2 characters
second --> first: 3 possible lengths
first -> second: length 0 leaves 3 characters
second --> first: 4 possible lengths
@enduml

resource_chain.label: A defect becomes a service failure through resource use
resource_chain.description: Overlapping repetition in a backtracking pattern permits excessive search. With triggering input and inadequate protection, resource demand interferes with serving requests. Failed request handling becomes visible as 502 errors. This causal model distinguishes a defective implementation choice, an incorrect runtime condition relative to a resource requirement, and an external failure.
resource_chain.caption: A hot CPU alone is not a diagnosis. State the progress or resource requirement that the execution violates.
resource_chain.source:
@startuml
layout vertical
component OverlappingRepetition
component ExcessiveSearch
component ImpairedRequestProgress
component Visible502
OverlappingRepetition --> ExcessiveSearch : triggering input
ExcessiveSearch --> ImpairedRequestProgress : insufficient protection
ImpairedRequestProgress --> Visible502 : service cannot complete
@enduml

repaired_model.label: A single forward scan for the teaching contract
repaired_model.description: The proposed teaching repair inspects the next unexamined character. Equals leads to Found. A different character advances to the next character. End of input leads to Absent. No transition revisits an earlier character. This is a specification for the tiny equals-search exercise, not a replacement for Cloudflare's security rule.
repaired_model.caption: Preserve the required answer while changing the search structure. This model inspects each input character at most once.
repaired_model.source:
@startuml
state InspectNext
state Advance
state Found
state Absent
[*] --> InspectNext
InspectNext --> Found : equals found
InspectNext --> Advance : other character
Advance --> InspectNext : next unexamined position
InspectNext --> Absent : end of input
@enduml

safeguards.label: Different safeguards interrupt different causal links
safeguards.description: A rule enters performance testing, then staged deployment, then request matching. Bounded matching and runtime resource protection limit work at evaluation. A recovery path provides a way to remove a problematic rule. These are conceptual responsibilities drawn from the response measures, not a claim that every measure had already shipped in July 2019.
safeguards.caption: Prevent expensive work, contain rollout exposure, and preserve recovery access. These are complementary obligations.
safeguards.source:
@startuml
layout vertical
component Rule
component PerformanceTests
component StagedRollout
component BoundedMatching
component RecoveryPath
Rule --> PerformanceTests : challenge cost
PerformanceTests --> StagedRollout : limit initial exposure
StagedRollout --> BoundedMatching : serve requests
RecoveryPath --> BoundedMatching : remove problematic rule
@enduml

restoration.label: Three milestones establish different claims
restoration.description: Traffic recovered at 14:09 UTC on 2 July. WAF service was restored at 14:52 after the bad rule was removed and isolated checks were performed. A later engine change in July 2019 is retrospectively confirmed by a 2020 article. This milestone diagram is not a complete release history or software state machine.
restoration.caption: Recovery, restoration, and later hardening are distinct milestones. The follow-up confirms the engine migration; a target date alone would not.
restoration.source:
@startuml
state TrafficRecovered
state WAFRestored
state EngineChanged
TrafficRecovered --> WAFRestored : 14:52 UTC on July 2
WAFRestored --> EngineChanged : later in July 2019
note left of TrafficRecovered : 14:09 UTC on July 2
note right of EngineChanged : Confirmed in 2020 account
@enduml

transfer.label: A new incident with an unknown expensive component
transfer.description: Uploads pass through a validator, then a report builder, before a result is returned. After a rule update, large uploads time out and CPU is high. The diagram does not identify which component consumes the CPU or whether the update caused the timeout. This is an invented transfer scenario.
transfer.caption: New scenario: preserve the debugging method while withholding the diagnosis. No regex defect has been established here.
transfer.source:
@startuml
layout vertical
component Uploads
component Validator
component ReportBuilder
component Result
Uploads --> Validator : inspect content
Validator --> ReportBuilder : accepted records
ReportBuilder --> Result : build report
note right of Uploads : Large uploads time out
@enduml
